title: Phòng Trữ Đồ: build a full-stack app with TypeScript, Node.js and React

parts.title: Setup and how this course works
parts.goal: Install everything and learn the red-green loop.

exercises.title: Hello, tests
exercises.goal: Nothing to write: run `npm run check` and watch it pass. This proves Node, TypeScript and Vitest work and that the `@/` import alias reaches your `src/` folder.
hints: Run the tests in watch mode with `npm run test:watch` and edit a file.
Find the `@` alias in vitest.config.ts and tsconfig.json.

manual.text: I ran `npm run check` and saw exercise 0.1 pass
I know `solutions/` holds spoilers and `src/` is where I work
I can explain what `npm run typecheck` does that the tests do not

parts.title: The domain in TypeScript
parts.goal: Model an item and write the first rules: dates, expiry and the month-vs-last-month spending comparison.

milestone.text: Your room has a first report: spending and what is about to expire.
milestone.run: npm run room -- seed && npm run room

exercises.title: Types and the item factory
exercises.practice: Model an item and validate input
exercises.goal: Write a type guard (`value is CategoryId`), a lookup that cannot return undefined, and `makeItem`, which validates input and fills defaults.
hints: `CATEGORY_IDS as readonly string[]` lets `.includes` accept any string. Why is that cast needed?
Throw early: validate every field before building the object.

exercises.title: Dates without surprises
exercises.practice: Parse, format and compare calendar days
exercises.goal: Six small functions. The lesson: `new Date('2026-11-08')` is UTC, `new Date(2026, 10, 8)` is local, and `toISOString` is always UTC.
hints: Months are 0-based in `new Date(y, m, d)`.
After building a Date, read it back: if the day changed, the input was invalid (Feb 31).

exercises.title: Expiry status
exercises.practice: Combine small functions into app rules
exercises.goal: Classify items (none, ok, soon, expired), write the human text, and build the list the notification panel shows.
hints: `Array.prototype.sort` mutates. What do you call before sorting to avoid that?
Return early for the special cases (negative, 0, 1) before the general message.

exercises.title: Spending comparison
exercises.practice: Group by month and compare with last month
exercises.goal: Format Vietnamese dong with `Intl`, total a month, and compare this month so far with the same days of last month (including the January to December wrap).
hints: `new Date(year, month + 1, 0).getDate()` is the number of days in `month`.
Write `totalForMonth` first; `compareSpending` is three calls to it.

manual.text: I ran the milestone command and the Spending and Needs attention sections are unlocked
I can explain `string` vs a literal union vs `unknown`
I can explain why functions take `today` as a parameter
I can name one way UTC and local time differ in `Date`

parts.title: Rules of the room
parts.goal: Teach the app to think: same-product detection, the rebuy rule, dormant items and category guessing.

milestone.text: You can add items from the terminal: the category is guessed, buying milk again retires last month's milk, and idle things are reported.
milestone.run: npm run room -- add "Sữa tươi tiệt trùng" --price 33000 && npm run room

exercises.title: Are these the same product?
exercises.practice: Normalise text and compare word sets
exercises.goal: Remove accents with `normalize('NFD')`, split names into meaningful words and decide with set arithmetic.
hints: `đ` does not decompose; replace it by hand.
Intersection and union sizes are enough for both rules.

exercises.title: The rebuy rule
exercises.goal: When you buy something again, last month's copy leaves the room. Return new objects, never mutate.
hints: `{ ...older, used: true }` copies an object.
Use a Map from id to its replacement and `items.map(i => map.get(i.id) ?? i)`.

exercises.title: Dormant items
exercises.goal: Find items nobody touched for a long time, with different thresholds per category and a snooze.
hints: Read the doc comment of `isDormant` as a list of early returns.
`needsAsk` is one line if `isDormant` and `inDate` exist.

exercises.title: Guess the category
exercises.goal: Match whole words in Vietnamese. `\b` only understands ASCII, so build the boundary yourself with `\p{L}` and the `u` flag.
hints: Look-around is not needed: capture groups on both sides are enough for `test`.
Cache each category's RegExp in a Map; building a RegExp is not free.

manual.text: I ran the milestone command and saw a guessed category and the rebuy message
I can write a regex that matches whole Vietnamese words and say why `\b` fails
I can explain `normalize('NFD')`
I know which of map, filter, sort, reverse, push mutate the array

parts.title: Reading bills
parts.goal: Turn the text of a bill into items: supermarket receipts, Shopee orders and café tables.

milestone.text: You can import real bills from the terminal.

exercises.title: Reading money
exercises.practice: Parse numbers as printed on Vietnamese bills
exercises.goal: `72.000` is seventy-two thousand, `12,5` is twelve and a half. Two tiny parsers with big consequences.
hints: Test the dot-thousands pattern first.
`parseInt(x, 10) || 0` turns NaN into 0.

exercises.title: Supermarket receipt parser
exercises.goal: One product per line, price at the end. Skip totals and taxes (in English and Vietnamese) without skipping real products.
hints: Slice the price off the end first, then look for the quantity in what is left.
Dates set `bought` for all rows, so collect it while looping and apply it at the end.

exercises.title: Online order parser (Shopee)
exercises.goal: A product spans three lines; a 'Thành tiền' line closes a group and spreads the real total across it.
hints: Keep three variables: the previous line, the current product and the products waiting for a total.
Check for a price line before the generic 'remember this as the product name' fallback.

exercises.title: Café receipt parser
exercises.goal: Parse a table, attach free toppings to the line above and scale prices to the grand total.
hints: Name the capture groups in comments before writing the regex.
Rounding: `Math.round(grand * price / sum)`.

exercises.title: Pick the right parser
exercises.goal: Detect the bill format and call the right parser. Order matters because a café bill also contains 'Thành tiền'.
hints: A `switch` over a union lets TypeScript prove you covered every case.

manual.text: I ran the milestone command on all three files in samples/
I can pass a function as a parameter to make code testable (`guess`)
I can explain why `72.000` and `12,5` need different handling

parts.title: A Node.js backend
parts.goal: Put the rules behind a REST API with validation and a JSON file for storage.

milestone.text: A server that other programs (and soon your browser) can talk to. It uses the same data/items.json as the terminal.
milestone.run: npm run server   (then, in another terminal: curl localhost:3001/api/summary)

exercises.title: In-memory store
exercises.goal: A tiny repository class that hands out copies and notifies when data changes.
hints: Spread (`{ ...item }`) makes a shallow copy; items only hold primitives so that is enough.
Only call `emit()` when something actually changed.

exercises.title: Saving to a file
exercises.practice: Async file I/O and atomic writes
exercises.goal: Load and save JSON with `fs/promises`. A missing file is fine on the first run; a broken file must NOT silently become an empty room.
hints: `error.code === 'ENOENT'` identifies a missing file.
Write to `path.tmp`, then `rename`: rename is atomic.

exercises.title: Validating requests with zod
exercises.goal: Describe request bodies as zod schemas. The TypeScript type is derived from the schema, so they cannot drift apart.
hints: `z.enum` accepts a readonly tuple like CATEGORY_IDS.
`.optional()` makes a key optional; `.trim().min(1)` rejects blank names.

exercises.title: Express routes
exercises.practice: HTTP verbs, status codes, error middleware
exercises.goal: Wire the domain functions into a REST API and test it with supertest, without opening a port.
hints: Let `schema.parse` throw; one error middleware turns ZodError into a 400.
Use 201 for create, 204 for delete (no body) and 404 for unknown ids.

manual.text: I ran the server and called it with curl
I can explain what 200, 201, 204, 400 and 404 mean
I can explain why validation lives at the edge (the route) and the domain trusts its types
I can explain why `loadItems` rethrows errors other than 'file not found'

parts.title: React: the first screens
parts.goal: Build the visual pieces: spending card, attention list, add-item form and the room.

milestone.text: Every component is visible in the gallery, with example data.

exercises.title: Spending card
exercises.goal: A pure view of a `SpendingComparison`. Accessibility roles (`region`, `status`) make it testable and usable.
hints: Build the change text in a small helper above the JSX.

exercises.title: Needs-attention list
exercises.practice: Derived data and lists with keys
exercises.goal: Render the notification list from props. No state and no effect: compute during render.
hints: Do not store `needsAttention(...)` in state; it is derived from props.
The `key` must be stable and unique: use the item id.

exercises.title: The add-item form
exercises.goal: A controlled form with validation. Tests use Testing Library: they find things by label and role, the way users and screen readers do.
hints: `<label htmlFor>` must match the input's `id`, or `getByLabelText` fails.
`event.preventDefault()` stops the browser from reloading the page.

exercises.title: The room
exercises.goal: Show the items that are still in the room as buttons placed with percentages. (Dragging comes in part 6.)
hints: `aria-pressed` expects a boolean-ish value.
Filter out used items before mapping.

manual.text: I opened the gallery and every section is unlocked
I can explain controlled vs uncontrolled inputs
I can explain why derived data should not live in state
I can explain what `key` does

parts.title: State and interaction
parts.goal: Manage the list of items with a reducer, then make the room interactive with dragging.

milestone.text: You can pick up items and move them around the room in the gallery.
milestone.run: npm run dev   (open /#gallery and drag an item)

exercises.title: The items reducer
exercises.goal: All the ways the room can change, in one pure function with a discriminated union of actions.
hints: Inside `case 'added':` TypeScript knows `action.item` exists.
Return the same array when nothing changed so React can skip a render.

exercises.title: Dragging maths
exercises.goal: Convert pointer positions into room percentages. Pure maths is easy to test and easy to reuse in the component later.
hints: `(clientX - box.left) / box.width * 100`.
`Math.round(v * 10) / 10` rounds to one decimal.

exercises.title: Drag an item around the room
exercises.goal: Extend your Room: press an item, move the pointer, release, and report the drop with `onMove(id, x, y)`. While dragging, draw the item under the pointer. A drag must not count as a click.
hints: Keep `drag` in state (it changes what is drawn) but 'did the pointer move?' in a ref (changing it must not re-render).
Put onPointerMove / onPointerUp on the container, not on the button: a fast pointer leaves the button.
jsdom has no layout: the test fakes getBoundingClientRect. Read the room's box from a ref.

manual.text: I dragged an item in the gallery
I can explain why a reducer must not mutate its state
I can explain when to use a ref instead of state

parts.title: Connecting to the server
parts.goal: Write the client for your API, the hook that keeps the screen in sync, and the App that ties it together.

milestone.text: The app works end to end in your browser, backed by your server.
milestone.run: npm run server   and   npm run dev   (open http://localhost:5173)

exercises.title: Typed API client
exercises.goal: One `request` helper that handles JSON, errors and 204. The `fetch` function is a parameter, so tests pass a fake.
hints: `response.ok` is false for 4xx and 5xx; fetch only rejects on network failure.
Call `response.json()` inside try/catch: an error page may not be JSON.

exercises.title: useItems hook
exercises.goal: Load on mount, add after the server answers, move and remove optimistically and undo by reloading when the server says no.
hints: Wrap functions in `useCallback` so their identity is stable.
A `cancelled` flag in the effect cleanup prevents updates after unmount.

exercises.title: Put it all together
exercises.goal: Combine the hook and the components into the screen: loading and error states, spending, attention list, room, and the add-item form.
hints: Hooks must run in the same order every render: call `useItems` and `useState` BEFORE any early return.
Derive `selected` from `selectedId` instead of storing the whole item.

manual.text: I added an item in the browser and found it in data/items.json
I can explain optimistic updates and when to roll back
I can explain why `fetch` does not throw on a 404

parts.title: Finishing touches
parts.goal: The last features that make it the real Phòng Trữ Đồ: Miso and Misu, drag-to-save, delete and importing a bill from the browser.

milestone.run: npm run server   and   npm run dev   (open http://localhost:5173)

exercises.title: What Miso and Misu say
exercises.goal: A pure function that looks at the room and returns what the cat (money and dates) and the dog (forgotten things) say today. Pure rules, no UI.
hints: Write Miso's rules as early returns, in the order of the doc comment.
Misu uses `dormantList(items, today)[0]` and `idleDays`.

exercises.title: The Mascots panel
exercises.goal: Show the messages from 8.1: one `<article>` per pet with its mood in `data-mood`.
hints: `aria-label` on an `<article>` gives it an accessible name.
No state, no effect: call `mascotMessages` while rendering.

exercises.title: Import a bill
exercises.practice: A small multi-step UI with async calls
exercises.goal: Paste bill text, read it through the server, review the rows (untick the ones you do not want) and add the rest.
hints: State you need: the text, the rows, the format, which rows are ticked (a Set of indexes), busy and error.
`try/catch/finally` around the await: `finally` is where `busy` goes back to false.
Reset `checked` to every index when new rows arrive.

exercises.title: The finished App
exercises.practice: Extending a component you wrote earlier
exercises.goal: Add the new pieces to your App: pets at the top, drag-to-move that saves, a Delete button for the selected item, and the bill import panel. When this is green, you have the whole app.
hints: `move` already exists in `useItems` (7.2): pass it to Room as onMove.
The bill panel is shown only when `api.parseBill` exists.
Import rows one by one with `await add(...)`; leave `exp` out when it is an empty string.

manual.text: I imported samples/shopee.txt through the browser
I moved an item, reloaded the page and it stayed there
I can name two things I would add next (a real database, photo reading, login, deploying)
